title: Inference Decision Framework for Prospects (Commercial Playbook)
author: Laura Chen
audience: Sales executives, solutions engineers, AE/SDR teams working Qualified and Early-Stage Enterprise accounts
summary: A structured, tactical commercial playbook that helps sales and solutions teams diagnose a prospect's inference needs, position Redwood's unique value, run a lightweight TCO and risk comparison, and close with tailored pricing and security points. Includes competitive brief, pitch outline, three short case vignettes, and a prospect-facing security FAQ.
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a repeatable decision framework and companion collateral for sellers and solutions engineers engaging mid-market and enterprise buyers evaluating LLM inference platforms. This doc prioritizes lifecycle risks (cost, latency, reliability, compliance) and gives concrete talk tracks, objection responses, and example pricing scenarios.

How to use this playbook
1) Qualification checklist (5 minutes): use during initial discovery call. If 3+ boxes checked, recommend a Technical Brief and Demo.
   - Expected concurrent requests > 20 QPS or bursty spikes > 100 QPS
   - Hard latency SLOs (p99 < 500ms) for interactive flows
   - Data residency, audit, or regulatory controls needed (HIPAA, PCI, GDPR localized data)
   - Budget sensitivity where per-token economics matter (high volume generation or embeddings)
   - Multi-cloud or private deployment preference

2) Rapid diagnosis (10–30 minutes with SE): map prospect to one of three buyer archetypes below to tailor messaging and pricing.

Buyer archetypes
- Developer-first startup (PLG flow): Prioritizes time-to-value, simple hosted API, cost transparency, sample-based benchmarks.
- Product team at scale (SaaS): Requires predictable throughput, predictable pricing (Reserved/Dedicated), and rollout controls.
- Regulated enterprise (Finance/Healthcare/Gov): Needs Private/VPC, KMS/HSM, audit trail, compliance evidence and professional services.

Positioning & Talk tracks (by archetype)
- Developer-first: "Ship quickly with our hosted API, free credits, and SDKs — benchmarked latency and cost profiles let you plan growth."
- Product team: "Lock predictable capacity and unit economics with Dedicated pools; integrate with Redwood Console for per-route observability and cost allocation."
- Regulated enterprise: "Deploy Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem bundle with KMS integration and SLA-backed support for regulated workloads."

Competitive brief (concise)
Use this as a one-page sheet when prospects ask how Redwood differs vs typical alternatives.

Competitors considered: Managed cloud AI endpoints, pure open-source self-hosted runtimes, and LLM API providers.

Comparison matrix (high level)
| Dimension                   | Redwood Inference                   | Managed Cloud Endpoints        | Open self-hosted runtimes         | LLM API provider (low-cost)    |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Time-to-value              | High (hosted + SDKs + templates)    | Medium                        | Low (build + ops)                 | High                           |
| Predictable cost           | High (Dedicated + Optimize tooling) | Low/Varies                    | Depends on operator               | Variable                       |
| Private deployment         | VPC/on-prem supported                | Limited                       | Supported but heavy ops           | Rare                           |
| Observability & rollout    | Native Console + per-route metrics   | Basic                        | Custom-built                      | Minimal                        |
| Compliance evidence        | Prebuilt artifacts & PS offering     | Varies                        | Depends on implementation         | Low                            |
| SLAs & enterprise support  | SLA-backed (Dedicated/Private)       | Varies                        | No vendor SLA                     | Limited                        |

Key competitive messages to use in sales calls
- "We are inference-first: our runtime and orchestration optimize latency and cost specifically for LLM workloads, not generic CPU/GPU endpoints."
- "Unified experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — reduces your integration and operational complexity."
- "You can start hosted for speed and migrate to Dedicated or Private with preserved API and tooling."

Pitch deck outline (10–12 slides, quick sequence)
1. Title / TL;DR — one-sentence value prop and fit (30s)
2. Customer problem — latency, cost, reliability, and compliance gaps (1–2 slides)
3. Redwood solution overview — runtime + routing + tooling (1 slide)
4. Deployment paths — Hosted, Dedicated, Private with example personas (1 slide)
5. Measured outcomes — benchmark snapshots: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (1 slide)
6. Security & compliance highlights — KMS, VPC, audit logs (1 slide)
7. Pricing models & example TCO (1–2 slides)
8. 30/60/90 pilot plan — success criteria and checkpoints (1 slide)
9. Case vignettes — 2 short wins (1 slide)
10. Next steps & ask — trial, POC scope, stakeholders (1 slide)

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb and example scenarios)
- Pricing levers: hosted per-token, embeddings units, dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), professional services (onboarding/validation), retention/observability add-ons.
- Rules of thumb:
  * For experimental/low-volume projects: recommend hosted API with monthly spend cap and SDK guides.
  * For predictable product features (>=$10k/month): propose Dedicated pooled capacity to achieve predictable latency and lower unit cost.
  * For regulated workloads: price Private deployment as a platform fee + annual support + optional on-prem binpack.

Example TCO (simple worksheet):
- Prospect A: 2M generated tokens/month, 50k embeddings/month, interactive product with target p95 < 600ms.
  * Hosted: $0.25 per 1k tokens = $500/month + embeddings $0.10 per 1k = $5/month => baseline $505/mo (but variable).
  * Dedicated (example): Reserved pool $6,000/mo amortized, yields 4x lower per-token marginal cost at scale + priority capacity => suggests break-even at ~25M tokens/month.
Notes: use our internal pricing calculator for precise quotes; provide 3 options (pilot hosted, reserved 3-month, reserved 12-month) in proposals.

Sample collateral snippets (ready-to-use talk tracks)
- Objection: "Why not host ourselves?" Response: "You can, but our runtime reduces operator lift by providing optimized kernels, continuous batching, KV caching, and automated fallbacks — that typically accelerates time-to-safe-production by 3–6 months and lowers ops headcount."
- Objection: "What's the migration path from hosted to private?" Response: "Same API and rollout primitives — we migrate config and model versions; we run a staged canary and provide runbook/hand-off sessions."

Three short case vignettes (high-level, anonymized)
1) Fintech data enrichment platform — outcome: moved from self-hosted model to Redwood Dedicated; reduced per-token cost by 48% and achieved p99 latency 420ms under 60 QPS bursts.
2) B2B SaaS support automation — outcome: shipped chat assistant via Hosted API in 2 weeks; reduced average handle time by 22% and increased CSAT by 8 points after pilot.
3) Healthcare analytics partner — outcome: Private deployment with HSM-backed KMS and audit pipeline; passed internal compliance review and enabled production PHI handling with contractual BAAs.

Pilot plan template (30/60/90)
- 0–30 days: kickoff, access, sample dataset ingest, baseline benchmark (latency/cost/quality), success metrics defined.
- 31–60 days: integration of SDKs, instrument Redwood Console dashboards, run canary traffic, iterate prompts and quantization profile.
- 61–90 days: scale traffic, finalize routing policies, hand-off to SRE/Platform, debrief and contract signature.

Prospect-facing Security FAQ (concise answers for initial meetings)
Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: Hosted: region-selectable cloud regions; Dedicated: customer-exclusive pools within provider region; Private: customer-managed VPC or on-prem.

Q: Can you sign a BAA or SOC2 addendum?
A: Yes — Redwood has PS engagement options and SOC2 artifacts; BAAs are available for Private deployments.

Q: How do you manage encryption keys?
A: Integrated KMS support for cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments; bring-your-own-key (BYOK) supported.

Q: Do you log raw requests or PII?
A: By default, minimal telemetry is retained for billing and SLOs; options to disable request retention and anonymize logs are available under contract.

Q: What controls exist for model updates and rollbacks?
A: Redwood supports pinned model versions, canary/A-B rollout policies, and automatic fallback to compatible variants. Audit trails capture all rollout events.

Enablement artifacts (attachments and templates to use)
- One-page competitive brief (PDF) — use the "Comparison matrix" section as source.
- 10-slide pitch deck template (editable) — includes the 30/60/90 pilot slide and TCO worksheet.
- Pricing worksheet (Google Sheet) — three tabs: pilot, reserved, private.
- Security FAQ short-sheet for prospects (two-pager).

Operational playbook for SEs: step-by-step during a POC
1. Pre-engagement: request sample traffic and SLAs, create a dedicated test project in Console.
2. Baseline test: run 1k synthetic requests and measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, concurrency behavior.
3. Performance tuning: suggest batching windows, quantization profile, and caching rules.
4. Review & sign-off: present results, present pricing options, and agree on success criteria.

Appendix: useful metrics and thresholds
- p50 / p95 / p99 latencies — target p99 < 500ms for interactive products.
- Cost per 1M tokens — tracked in Console; use Optimize recommendations to reduce cost by 15–40%.
- Embedding throughput — target 200–1000 embeddings/sec on Dedicated pool depending on GPU type.
